independentSourceInventory.sourceObservation: The original PNG shows one circuit subfigure. Reading the main horizontal line from left to right gives marked A, rectangular r1, marked B, rectangular r2, an unmarked intervening wire, rectangular r3, marked C, then a plain wire to marked D. No wire passes through a resistor body as an unintended short, and no branch leaves the r2-r3 connection.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Preserved in the spec and each actual-width preview.

independentSourceInventory.sourceObservation: A second path descends from B, runs right through rectangular r4, and rises to C. Its resistor sits approximately beneath r3. This is a resistor-bearing BC bypass around r2 and r3 together, not around r1 and not an ammeter shunt.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Both BC alternatives remain connected at B and C only; r1 remains upstream of both. Modern spacing is uncalibrated, not resistance-dependent.

independentSourceInventory.sourceObservation: Four filled node marks are labelled A and D below the main line and B and C above it. Resistor labels r1, r2 and r3 are below their main-line rectangles; r4 is below the lower rectangle. The original uses subscript numerals and carries no numeric component values.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: All labels retain their identities and sides. ASCII r1/r2/r3/r4 is a clear notation regularization of the written r-subscript symbols, not a new value.

independentSourceInventory.sourceObservation: Above the circuit, a horizontal span labelled V has a left-pointing arrowhead by the upright guide over A and a right-pointing arrowhead by the guide over D. These opposing heads annotate terminal voltage, not current flow. There is no meter circle, battery symbol or polarity sign in the source.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: The modern figure preserves outward directions and thin endpoint guides without adding a supply, meter or conducting bypass to the declared circuit topology. V is a voltage-span label and A is a node label, neither a meter designation.

independentSourceInventory.sourceObservation: A small isolated diagonal ink mark floats above r3 in the original; it has no connection, readable label or arrowhead. The original has no numerical current, voltage-drop, power or dimensional annotation.
independentSourceInventory.comparison: Omitting the isolated mark and scan texture removes no source component or relationship. No numerical givens or calculated answers were introduced into the image.

requestedQuantities: heat released per second in r1, denoted P
sourceStem.candidateModel: Constant ohmic resistances, negligible connecting-wire resistance and steady direct current.
sourceStem.geometryBasis: Original PNG topology and labels plus the written exercise stem. No geometry, resistor length, arrow direction or figure annotation was inferred from the worked solution or calculated answer.
sourceStem.valueFidelity: The source drawing is symbolic. Retaining its symbolic labels is consistent with all stem values and does not require duplicating those values inside the figure.
sourceStem.contextRetention: The complete exercise3 candidate text is retained byte-consistently in the context and spec. Its worked solution is context only and remains under the existing SCI review.

observations.currentPathsAndMeterScope: Tracing only conducting source wires gives r1 between A and B; r2 then r3 along the upper BC route; r4 along the lower BC route; and an unobstructed C-D wire. There are no current-direction arrows or meter labels to translate. Neither terminal-voltage guide nor its span is treated as a conducting current path.
observations.labelsAndAppearance: Visible labels are exactly A, B, C, D, r1, r2, r3, r4 and V. They use Latin symbols and numerals, with no Cyrillic, Chinese, cultural decoration or answer-bearing additions. All requested previews are nonblank and preserve clear separation between labels, leads, component outlines and arrowheads.
